content:
alex: throwing this here in case others hit it: our Go generator quickstart confuses users when they cancel context during startup. sample app shows Next(ctx) loop but ctor uses background ctx for initial handshake so Close() can hang. reproducible with go 1.20 + go-sdk v0.14.x on mac/linux.

jamie: can you paste the minimal repro? curious if it's oauth retry related or just the stream handshake.

alex: minimal snippet below. behavior: Next(ctx) exits after cancel but gen.Close() blocks until the timeout. pprof shows goroutines in a token refresh/backoff loop.
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
gen := client.Generator("gpt-open")
go func(){ time.Sleep(100*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for gen.Next(ctx) { fmt.Println(gen.Value().Text) }
// stalls here
if err := gen.Close(); err != nil { log.Printf("close error: %v", err) }
```

kai: thanks. we've seen this across a few reports. root cause: handshake (and any token refresh retries) is spawned with context.Background(), so cancellation on the iterator ctx doesn't reach it. Close waits for that background worker to finish.

jamie: two practical options: (A) make Generator accept a handshake ctx (e.g., NewGenerator(ctx, opts...)) or through a functional option `WithHandshakeCtx(ctx)`; (B) add CloseWithContext/Close(ctx) so callers can bound shutdown. both are small API surface changes and solve most real-world cases.

alex: +1 for exposing Close(ctx). I think that avoids breaking callers and fixes CI flakes quickly. we should still make the runtime respect ctx for token refresh though.

kai: agreed. runtime change: ensure token source backoff/retry selects on ctx.Done() when waiting between attempts. will add a unit test that injects a slow token source and asserts early cancellation unblocks the handshake.

doc-bot: created ticket DE-2609 "go: generator ctor uses background ctx; Close blocks on auth/handshake retries" https://tracker/internal/DE-2609 :white_check_mark:

jamie: devex action: update quickstart sample to show both patterns and a cancellation note. new quickstart snippet should show either passing a derived ctx into ctor or using Close(ctx) to protect shutdown. also show the callback-style generator example which threads ctx differently.

alex: filed a tiny repro gist: https://gist.github.com/alex/go-gen-cancel-repro that includes a unit test `TestGeneratorCancel` for folks to run locally.

kai: i'll open a draft PR with three parts: thread token refresh on user ctx, add Close(ctx) (non-breaking by keeping Close() for now), and add tests. jamie, can you update the quickstart in the same PR? smaller patch so we can backport a doc tweak to the website.

jamie: will do. i'll also add a short migration blurb for v0.14 -> v0.15 noting the Close(ctx) and handshake-ctx change.

ci-bot: linked PR #4021 to DE-2609. automated CI will run generator e2e with simulated auth delays.

alex: awesome, thanks all. this was tripping a couple of new hires during onboarding today so glad we have a clear plan. :relieved:
